privacy.ai_training_note: Trains on customer prompts, inputs, and outputs BY DEFAULT for Playground (consumer) and standard FLUX API use. Privacy policy: content 'submitted to the Services, such as your image files, and the output that is created' is used to 'develop, train and improve the Services, including to research, develop, train and otherwise improve... our AI models.' FLUX API Service Terms grant BFL a 'royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive and fully sublicensable' license to use Input and Output to train and improve its AI models. KEY EXCEPTION: the privacy policy 'does not apply to information that we process as a processor or service provider on behalf of our business customers', i.e., where BFL is a data processor under contract. Enterprise/bespoke contracts offer 'rights not available in standard terms' and may include non-training. No 'zero retention' default exists for standard API. Self-hosted Open Weights keep data on the customer's own infrastructure (BFL never receives it).
privacy.data_region: International transfers under EU Standard Contractual Clauses; no published data-residency guarantee. BFL is a German lab (Freiburg) with a US entity (Black Forest Labs, Inc.); infrastructure runs on Microsoft Azure.

security.name: CSAM/NSFW safety filtering
security.value: Pre-training data filtered for NSFW and known CSAM; partnered with the Internet Watch Foundation to filter known CSAM. Model repositories also include NSFW and IP-infringing content filters at input and output, and BFL ran a third-party red-team evaluation (~2,800 T2I/I2I prompts) before release.
security.proof_quote: Black Forest Labs filtered the pre-training data for multiple categories of 'not safe for work' (NSFW) and known child sexual abuse material (CSAM) ... partnered with the Internet Watch Foundation ... to filter known CSAM from the training data.

products.name: Playground (consumer / no-code web)
products.data_scope: Full privacy policy applies; prompts, images, and outputs may be used to train BFL AI models.
products.notes: Highest data-sharing posture; not appropriate for confidential inputs.

products.name: FLUX API
products.data_scope: Standard service terms grant BFL rights to use Input/Output to train and improve models. No default zero-retention.
products.notes: For business customers where BFL acts as a processor under contract, training exemptions apply; confirm via signed agreement/DPA.

products.name: Open Weights / Self-hosted (Hugging Face, GitHub, license)
products.data_scope: Runs entirely on the customer's own infrastructure; BFL does not receive prompts or outputs.
products.notes: Best privacy posture. FLUX.1 [dev] is non-commercial license; commercial/self-hosted needs a paid license.

products.name: Enterprise
products.data_scope: Bespoke terms; 'rights not available in standard terms'; may include non-training and custom retention.
products.notes: Requires Contact Sales; ISO 27001 + SOC 2 Type II + GDPR posture supports enterprise diligence.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium playground + usage-based API pricing + per-license open-weights/self-hosted + bespoke enterprise
compare.data_residency: No residency guarantee on hosted; EU SCCs for transfers. Self-hosted = full customer control.

flags: Trains on customer prompts/inputs/outputs by default for Playground and standard API; material for anyone sending confidential or brand-sensitive imagery.
Training exemption exists only where BFL is a contracted processor (business customers) or under bespoke enterprise terms.
Self-hosting Open Weights is the only way to fully avoid sending data to BFL.

Source evidence file contained a mis-scraped privacy policy pointing to clay.com (an unrelated vendor); the correct BFL policy is https://bfl.ai/legal/privacy-policy, flagged so the directory does not ingest the wrong URL.
DPA availability not explicitly published; processor relationship for business customers implies one exists but verify.
